# Preheating system description and testing

#

1 To assist coid starting, diesel engines are fitted with a preheating system, which consists of a number of glow plugs (one per cylinder, a glow plug controal unit, a faciamounted warning lamp, a coolant temperature sensor mounted on the cylinder head, an ambient air temperature sensor mounted inside the giow plug contral unit, and the associated electrical wiring.

2 The glow plugs are miniature electric heating elements, encapsulated in a metal case with a probe at one end and electrical connection at the other. Each combustion chamber has one glow plug threaded into it, with the tip of the giow plug probe positioned directly in ine with incoming spray of fuel from the injectors. When the glow plug is energised, it heats up rapidly, causing the fuel passing over the glow plug probe to be heated to its optimum combustion tamperature, ready for combustion, in addition, same of the fuel passing over the glow plugs is ignited and this helps to trigger the combustion process.

3 The pre-heating systerm begins to operate as soan as the ignition key is switched to the second position, but only if the engine coolant temperature is below 60°C. A facia-mounted warning lamp informs the driver that preheating is taking place. The lamp extinguishes when sufficient preheating has taken place to allow the engine to be started. but power will stil be supplied to the glow plugs for a further period until the engine is started, If no attempt is made to start the engine, the power supply to the glow plugs is switched off after a period of time, to prevent battery drain and glow plug bum-out.

4 On 1.9 itre engines with conventional diesel inection systems, the duration of the preheating period is governed by the glow plug control unit. This device monitors the temperature of the air in the engine bay via a buit-in ambient air temperature sensor, then aiters the preheating time (the length for which the glow plugs are supplied with current) to suit the conditions. On 1.9 and 2.0 litre engines with electranically-contralled diesel injection systems, the glow plug control unit s operated by the injection system ECU, which determines the necessary preheating time based on inputs from the various system sensors.

5Post-heating takes place after the ignition key has been released from the "Start position; the glow plugs continue to operate for at least a further 15 seconds, heiping to improve fuel combustion whist the engine is warming up. resulting in quieter. smoather running and reduced exhaust emissions. The overal duration of the post-heating period s dependent on the coolant temperature, which is measured by a sensor mounted in the thermostat housing, and by engine speed which is determined by a switch, or a potentiometer on the jection pump control lever.

# 8 Manual transmission overhaul - general information

Overhauling a manual transmission is a difficult and involved job for the DiY home mechanic. In addition to dismanting and reassembling many small parts, clearances must be precisely measured and, i necessary. changed by selecting shims and spacers. internal transmission components are aiso often difficult to obtain, and in many instances, extremely expensive. Because of this, if the transmission develops a fault or becames noisy, the best course of action is to have the unit overhauled by a speciatist repairer, or to obtain an exchange reconditioned unit.

# General information

# 4 HP 14 transmission

1.8 and 2.0 litre petrol engine modeis are optionally available with a four-speed fulyautomatic tranamission, consisting of a torque converter, an epicyclic geartrain, and hydraulically-operated clutches and brakes (see illustration).

# AL4 type transmission

The AL4 transmission, optionally availabie on later 1.6 litre petrol engine modeis, is a development of the earler 4 HP 14 unit, and incorporates electronic control; the automatic gearchanges are electronically-controlled, rather than hydraulically as with the 4 HP 14 type. The advantage of electronic management is to provide a faster gearchange response. A kickdown facility is also provided, to enable a faster acceleration response when required.

# General information

1The starter inhibitor/reversing light switch is a dual-function switch which is screwed into the top of the transmission housing. The inhibitor function of the switch ensures that the engine can only be started with the selector ever in either the N or P positions, therefore preventing the engine being started with the transmission in gear. This is achieved by the switch cutting the supply to the starter motor solenoid. If at any time it is noted that the engine can be started with the seiector lever in any position other than P or N, thenit islikely that the inhibitor function of the switch is suspect. The switch also performs the function of the reversing ight switch. luminating the reversing ights whenever the selector lever is in the A position.

# General information

The braking system is of the servoassisted. dual-circuit hydraulic type. The arrangement of the hydraulic system is such that each circuit operates one frant and one rear brake from a tandem mastèr cylinder. Under normal circumstances. both circuits operate in unison. However, in the event of hydraulic failure in one circuit, full braking force will til be aaable at two wheels.

On ali modelis, the handbrake provides an independent mechanical means of rear brake application.

# General information

#

The independent front suspension is of the MacPherson strut type, incorporating coil springs and integral telescopic shock absorbers. The MacPherson struts are located by transverse lower suspension arms, which utise rubber inner mounting bushes, and incorporate a bailjoint at the outer ends. The front swivel hubs, which carry the wheel bearings, brake calipers and the hub/disc assemblies, are clamped to the MacPherson struts, and connected to the lower arns via the baljoints. A front anti-roll bar is fitted to all models. The antiroll bar is rubber-mounted onto the subframe, and is attached to the front suspension struts by a connecting ink on each side.

щ

The rear suspension is of the independent trailing arm type, which consists of two trailing arms, linked by a tubular crossmember. Torsion bars linking the trailing arms are situated in front of and behind the crossmember, and a stabiizer bar inking the arms passes through the centre of the crossmember.

The complete rear axie assembly is mounted onto the vehicle underbody by four self-steering' rubber mountings. These mountings are designed to move slightly under extreme cornering forces. This movement of the rear axle assembly has the effect of actually turning the rear wheels slightly, to help steer the vehicle in the required direction. This improves the handling of the vehicle when cornering at high speeds.

The steering column has a universal joint fitted in the centre of its length, which is connected to an intermediate shaft having a second universal joint at its lower end. The lower universal joint is clamped to the steering gear pinion by means of a pinch-bolt.

# Front swivel hub assembly - removal and refitting

The steering gear is mounted onto the front subframe, and is connected by two track rods, with baljoints at their outer ends, to the steering arms projecting rearwards from the swivel hubs. The track rods and baljoints are threaded, to facilitate toe setting adjustment.

# General information

The bodyshel is made of pressed-steel sections, and is available in three-door Coupe, five-door Hatchback, and five-door Estate versions. Most components are weided together, but some use is made of structural adhesives. The front wings are bolted on.

# 2 Maintenancebodywork and underframe

The general condition of a vehicie's bodywork is the one thing that significantly affects its value. Maintenance is easy, but needs to be regular. Neglect. particuiarly after minor damage, can lead quickly to further deterioration and costly repair bilis. It is important also to keep watch on those parts of the vehicle not immediately visible, for instance the underside, inside all the wheelarches, and the lower part of the engine compartment.

# 3 Maintenanceupholstery and carpets

Mats and carpets should be brushed or vacuum-cieaned regularly, to keep them free of grit. if they are badly stained, remove them from the vehicie for scrubbing or sponging. and make quite sure they are dry before refitting, Seats and interior trim paneis can be kept clean by wiping with a damp cloth and a proprietary upholstery cleaner. If they do become stained (which can be more apparent on light-coloured upholstery), use a littleliquid detergent and a soft nail brush to scour the grime out of the grain of the material. Do not forget to keep the headlining clean in the same way as the uphoistery. When using liquid cleaners inside the vehicle, do not overwet the surfaces being cleaned. Excessive damp could get into the seams and padded interior, causing stains, offensive odours or even rot. If the inside of the vehicle gets wet accidentally, it is worthwhile taking some trouble to dry it out properly, particularly where carpets are involved.

Caution: Do not leave oll or electric heaters inside the vehicie for this purpose.

Minor body damage - repair

вЩ

# Repairs of minor scratches in bodyworkork

It the scratch is very superficial, and does not penetrate to the metal of the bodywork. repair is very simple. Lightly rub the area of the scratch with a paintwork renovator, or a very fine cuting paste, to remove laose paint trom the scratch, and to ciear the surrounding bodywork of wax polish. Rinse the area with clean water.

# Repairs of dents in bodywork

When deep denting of the vehicle's bodywork has taken place, the first task is to pull the dent out, unti the affected bodywork aimost attains its original shape. There is litle point in trying to restore the original shape completely, as the metal in the damaged area wil have stretched on impact, and cannot be reshaped fully to its original contour. It is better to bring the level af the dent up to a point which is about 3 mm below the level of the surrounding bodywork. In cases where the dent is very shalliow anyway, it is not worth tying to pul it out at al if the underside of the dent is accessible, it can be hammered out gently from behind, using a mallet with a wooden or plastic head. Whilst doing this. hoid a suitable block of wood firmly against the outside of the panei, to absorb the impact from the hammer blows and thus prevent a large area of the bodywork from being "belledour'.

To complete the repair, see the Section on iling and respraying.

# Repairs of rust holes or gashes in bodyworrk

Remove all paint from the affected area, and from an inch or so of the surrounding 'sound' bodywork, using an abrasive pad or a wire brush on a power dil. If these are not available, a few sheets of abrasive paper will do the job most effectively. With the paint removed, you will be abie to judge the severity of the corrosion, and therefore decide whether to renew the whole panel (if this is possibie) or to repair the affected area. New body panels are not as expensive as most people think, and it is often quicker and more satisfactory to fit a new panel than to attempt to repair large areas of corosion.

# Bodywork repairs – filing and respraying

Before using this Section, see the Sections on dent, minor scratch, rust holes and gash repairs.

# Plastic components

Witn the use of more and more plastic body component y the ehicemanfacturersg bumpers. spoilers, and in some cases major body paneis), rectification of more serious damage to such items has become a matter of either entrusting repair work to a specialist in this field or renewing complete components. # 5Major body damage - repair

Where serious damage has occurred, or large areas need renewal due to neglect, it means that compiete new panels will need weiding-in, and this is best left to professionals. If the damage is due to impact, it wil also be necessary to check completely the alignment of the bodyshel, and this can only be carried out accurately by a Citroen deasier, or accident repair specialist, using special jigs. If the body is left misaligned, it is primarily dangerous, as the car will not handie properly, and secondly, uneven strasses will be imposed on the steering, suspension and possibly transmission, causing abnormal wear, or complete failure, particularly to such items as the tyres.

# General information and precautions

# Waring: Before carrying out any work on the electrical system, read through the precautions given in 'Safety first at the beginning of this manual, and in Chapter 5A.

The electrical system is of 12-volt negative earth type. Power for the lights and all electrical accessories is supplied by a leadacid type battery, which is charged by the atternator.

# Electrical fault indinggeneral information

Note: Refer to the precautions given in "Safety first' and in Section 1 of this Chapter before starting work. The foilowing fests relate to testing of the main electrical circuits, and should not be used to test delicate electronic circuits (such as engine management systems or anti-lock braking systems), particularly where an electronic control unit is used.

# General

1 A typical electrical circult consists of an electrical component, any switches, relays. motors, fuses, fusible links or circuit breakers related to that component, and the wiring and connectors which ink the component to both the battery and the chassis. To heip to pinpoint a probiem in an electrical circuit. wiring diagrams are included at the end of this Chapter.

# Finding an open-circuit

9 To check for an open-circuit, connect one lead of a circuit tester or voitmeter to either the negative battery terminal or a known good earth.

13 Cantinue to check the remainder of the circuit in the same fashion.

# Finding a short-circuit

15 To check tor a short-circuit, first disconnect the load(s) from the ciroult foads are the components which draw current from a circuit, such as bulbs, motors, heating elements, etc.

# Finding an earth fault

20 The battery negative terminal 1s connected to 'earth' - the metal of the engine/transmission and the car body - and most systems are wired so that they only receive a positive feed, the current returming via the metal of the car body. This means that the component mounting and the body form part of that circuit. Loose or corroded mountings can therefore cause a range of electrical faults, ranging from total failure of a circuit, to a puzzing partial fault. In particular, lights may shine dimly (especially when another circuit sharing the same earth point is in operation), motors (eg wiper motors or the radiator cooling fan mator) may run slowly. and the operation of one circuit may have an apparently-unrelated effect on another. Note that earth straps are used between certain components, such as the engine/transmission and the body, usually where there is no metal to-metal contact between components, due to flexible rubber mountings, etc.

# 3.3a For access to the fuses, remove the cover from the interiar fuse/relay box ...

use serrated washers between the terminal and the bodyshel, to ensure a clean and secure connection. When the connection is remade, prevent the onset of corosion in the future by applying a coat of petroleum jelly or silicone-based grease, or by spraying on (at regular intervals a proprietary inition seaer or water-dispersant lubricant.

# Fuses

1 Fusas are designed to break a circuit when a predetermined current is reached, in order to protect the components and wiring which could be damaged by excessive curent flow. Any excessive curent flow will be due to a fauit n the cirouit, usualy a short-circut (see Section 2.

of ighter gauge wiring and switch cantacts. A relay can receive more than one contr input, unike a mechanical switch. A relay can have a timer function - for example, the intermittent wicer ralav.

14To remove a relay, first ensure that th relevant circuit is switched off In most caset the reiay can then simply be pulled out fror the socket, and pushed back into position Note, however, that with the ever increasing standardisation of vehicle wiring and electrica system components, many relays are nor welded' in position in their relevant circui boards for ease of manufacture. This meane that the relays are soldered in place anc cannot be individually removed. If faulty. the complete circuit board or relay housing mus be renewed as an assembly. Changes of thit nature ocour regularly during the course o vehicle production and are not normally documented by the vehicle manufacturer. 20 Anti-theft alarm system and engine immobiliser general information

\*

# General

All models in the range are fitted with an anti-theft aiarm system as standard or optional equipment. The alarm is automaticaly armed and disarmed using the remote central locking transmitter (where applicable), When the system is activated, the alarm indicator light, located on the facia, wll flash continuously. In addition to the alarm function, the system also incorporates an angine immobiliser activated by a transponder in the ignition key.

# Anti-theft alarm system

Note that if the doors are operated using the key, the alarm will not be armed or disarmed (as applicabie),. If for some reason the remote central locking transmitter fails whilst the alarm is armed, the alarm can be disarmed using the key. To do this, open the door with the key, then anter the vehicle. noting that the alarm will sound as the door is opened. Switch on the ignitian, and once the ignition key is recognised, the alarm wil be disarmed.

# Engine immobiliser

An electronic engine immobiliser is incorporated as part of the anti-theft system. The electronic immobiliser consists of a transponder fitted to the ignition key, and an analogue module fitted around the ignition switch. The system is controlled by the passenger compartment body computer.

# Disconnecting the vehicle batery

Refer to Disconnecting the battery in the Reference Section of this manual).

21 Air bag system - general ifomation, precautions and system de-activation

# General information

A driver's air bag is fitted as standard equipment on certain models, and is an option an all other models. The air bag is fitted in the steering wheel centre pad. Additionally. a passenger's air bag located in the facia, and side air bags located in the front seats are also availabie.

# Precautions

A

system, to prevent the possiblity of personal injury.

# General precautions

The tollowing precautions must be observed when carrying out work on a vehicle equipped with an air bag:

# Precautions to be taken when handing an ar ba

aTransport the air bag by itsef, bag upward   
o not put your arms around the air bag.   
Cary the ar bag close to the body, bag outward.   
Do not drop the air bag or expose it to impacts.   
Do not attempt to dismantle the air beg unit.   
Do not connect any form of electrical equipment to any part of the air bag circult.

# Precautions to be taken when storing an air bag unit

a Store the unit in a cupboard with the air bag upward.   
Do not expose the air bag to temperatures above 80C.   
Do not expose the air bag to flames.   
Do not attempt to dispose of the air bag consult a Citron dealer.   
e Never refit an air bag which is known to be faulty or damaged.

# De-activation of air bag system

The system must be de-activated before carrying out any work on the air bag components or surrounding area:

### Choosing your engine oil
`citroen_xsara_en_b10720bd` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:62 | doc_type:owners_manual
Engines need of, not only to lubricate moving parts and minimise wear, but also to maximise power output and to improve fuel economy. By introducing a simplitied and improved range of engine oils, Duckhams has taken away the confusion and made it easier for you to choose the night ol for your engine.

### • Beating friction
`citroen_xsara_en_5d265d2f` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:63 | doc_type:owners_manual
Without oll the moving surtaces inside your engine will rub together, heat up and melt, quickly causing the engine to seize. Engine oil creates a fim which separates these moving parts, preventing wear and heat buld-up.

### 1 General information
`citroen_xsara_en_712a6615` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:188 | doc_type:owners_manual
This Chapter is designed to help the home mechanic maintain his/her vehicle for safety, ecanomy, long life and peak performance.

### Service interval display

Certain Xsara models are equipped with a service interval display indicator in the instrument panel, When the ignition is initially switched on, a spanner appears in the display window and the total number of miiee remaining untl che next senice is due, is also shown.

### Regular maintenance
`citroen_xsara_en_df16affc` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:190 | doc_type:owners_manual
1 I, from the time the vehicle is new, the routine maintenance schedule is followed closely, and frequent checks are made of fuid levels and nigh-wear items, as suggested throughout this manual, the engine willi be kept in relatively good running condition, and the need for additional work will be minimised. 2 It is possibie that there will be times when the engine is running poory due to the lack o! regular maintenance. This is even more likely if a used vehicle, which has not received regular and frequent maintenance checks, is purchased, in such cases, additional work imay need to be carried out, outside of the regular maintenance intervals.

b Check afl the engine-related fuds (see Weely checka).   
Check the fuel fiter (Sections 4 and 17).   
Check the condition of all hoses, and check for fluid leaka (Section 5).   
Check the conditon and tension of the auxllary drivebell (Section 6).   
Check the condition of the air fiter, and renew if necessary (Section 18).

### TU series engine description
`citroen_xsara_en_a36cb7de` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:281 | doc_type:owners_manual
The TU series engine is a well-proven engine wtich has been fitted to many previous Citroën and Peugeot vehicles. The engine is of the in-line four-cylinder, ovemead cershaf (OHC) type, mounted Iransversely at the front of the car,  with the transmission attached to its left-hand end. The Xsara range is, fited with both 1.4 Iire (13eacc) and 1.6 itre (1587cc) versions of the engine.

### Using this Chapter
`citroen_xsara_en_bdf735d2` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:344 | doc_type:owners_manual
This Part of Chapter 2 is devoted to in-car repair procedures for the XU series petrol engines. Similar information covering the TU series petrol engines, and the diesel engines will be found in Chapters 2A, 2C and 2D. All procedures concerning engine removal and refitting. and engine block/cylinder head overhaul for petrol and diesel engines can be found in Chapters 2E and 2F as applicable.

### XU series engine description
`citroen_xsara_en_76a1276d` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual
The XU series engine is a well-proven power unit which has been fited to many previous Citroin and Peugeot vehicles. The engine is of the in-line four-cylinder type. mounted transversely at the front of the car with the clutch and transmission attached to its left-hand end. The Xsara range is fitted with 1.8 litre (1761cc) and 2.0 litre (1998cc) engines. Both 8and 16-valve versions of the 1.8 litre engine are avalable, whereas all 2.0 itre engines are of 16-valve configuration.

`citroen_xsara_en_cf1ad609` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:433 | doc_type:owners_manual
This Part of Chapter 2 is devoted to in-car repair procedures for the XUD series diesel engines. Similar information covering the DW series diesel engines, and the petrol engines wil be found in Chapters 2A, 28 and 2D. Al procedures conceming engine removal and refiting, and engine block/cylinder head overhaul for petrol and diesel engines can be found in Chapters 2E and 2F as applicable.

### XUD series engine description
`citroen_xsara_en_08a671e5` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:434 | doc_type:owners_manual
The XUD series engine is a well-proven moder unit which has appeared in many Citroän and Peugeot vehicles. The engine is of four-cylinder overhead camshaft design, mounted transversely, with the transmission mounted on the left-hand side.

11 Check the timing belt carefully for any signs of uneven wear, split or ol contamination. Pay particular attention to the roots of the teeth. Renew it if there is the slightest doubt about its condition. If the engine is undergoing an overhaul, and has covered more than 40 000 miles (60 000 km) with the existing belt fitted, renew the belt as a matter of course, regardless of its apparent condition. The cost of a new bet is nothing compared with the cost of repairs, should the belt break in service. If signs of oil contamination are found, trace the source of the ail leak and rectify it. Wash down the engine timing belt area and all related camponents, to remove all traces of oi. Check that the tensioner and ider pulley rotates frely. without any sign of roughness. `citroen_xsara_en_e661193f` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:465 | doc_type:owners_manual
23The mating faces of the cylinder head and cylinder block/crankcase must be perfectly clean before refitting the head. Citron recommend the use of a scouring agent for this purpose, but acceptable results can be achieved by using a hard plastic or wood scraper to remove all traces of gasket and carbon. The same method can be used to clean the piston crowns. Take particular care to avoid scoring or gouging the cylinder head/cylinder block mating surfaces during the cleaning operations, as aluminium alioy is easily damaged. Make sure that the carbon is not aliowed to enter the oil and water passages - this is particularly important for the lubrication system, as carbon could biock the

### Using this Chapter
`citroen_xsara_en_99be079e` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:485 | doc_type:owners_manual
This Part of Chapter 2 is devoted to in-car repair procedures far the DW series diesei engines, Similar information covering the XUD series diesel engines, and the petrol engines wil be found in Chapters 2A, 28 and 2C. Al procedures conceming engine removal and refitting, and engine biock/cylinder head overhaul for petrol and diesel engines can be found in'Chapters 2E and 2F as applicable.

### DW series engine description
`citroen_xsara_en_f1dd14f0` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:486 | doc_type:owners_manual
The DW series engine is a relatively new power unit based on the well-proven XUD series engine which has appeared in many Ciron and Peugeot vehicles. The 1.9 itre (Dw8) engine is virtually identical to the 1. itre XUD unit apart from revisions to the cylinder head cover and fuel system components. The 2.0 itre (DWTD) engine i very similar to the XUD engine in terms of the cylinder block components, but the remainder of the engine has been compietely redesigned. Both engines are of four-cylinder single overhead camshaft design, mounted transversely, with the transmission mounted on the left-hand side.

### Repair operations – precaution
`citroen_xsara_en_70f2b21a` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:487 | doc_type:owners_manual
The 2.0 itre engine is a complex unit with numerous accessories and ancillary components. The design of the engine compartment is such that every conceivable space has been utilised, and access to virtually all of the engine components is extremely limited. In many cases, ancillary components will have to be removed, or moved to one side, and wiring. pipes and hoses will have to be disconnected or removed from various cable clips and support brackets.

### Preparation for refitting
`citroen_xsara_en_689773e2` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:548 | doc_type:owners_manual
18The mating faces of the cylinder head and cylinder biock/crankcase must be perfectly clean before refitting the head. Citron recommend the use of a scouring agent for this purpose, but acceptable resuits can be achieved by using a hard plastic or wood scraper to remove all traces of gasket and carbon. The same method can be used to clean the piston crowns. Take particular care to avoid scoring or gouging the cylinder head/cylinder block mating surfaces during the cleaning operatiors, as aluminium alloy is easily damaged. Make sure that the carbon is not allowed to enter the oll and water passages - this is particularly important for the lubrication system, as carbon could biock the oil supply to the engine's components. Using adhesive tape and paper, seal the water, oil and bolt holes in the cylinder block/crankcase. To prevent carbon entering the gap between the pistons and bores. smear a littie grease in the gap. After cieaning each piston, use a small brush to remove all traces of grease and carbon from the gap. then wipe away the remainder with a clean rag

25Carefully examine the cylinder head bolts for signs of damage to the threads or head. and for any sign of corrosion. If the bolts are in a satisfactory condition, measure the length of each boit from the underside of the head, to the end of the unthreaded portion at the base of the shank. 16The mating faces of the cylinder head and cylinder block must be perfectly clean before refitting the head. Citron recommend the use of a scouring agent for this purpose, but acceptable results can be achieved by using a hard plastic or wood scraper to remove all traces of gasket and carbon. The same method can be used to clean the piston crowns. Take particular care to avoid scoring or gouging the cylinder head/cylinder biock mating surfaces during the cleaning operations, as aluminium alloy is easily

### Gasket selection

19 Tum the crankshaft until pistons 1 and 4 are at TDC. Position a dial test indicator (dial gauge) on the cylinder block, and zero it on the block face. Transfer the probe to the edge of No 1 piston, then slowly tum the crankshaft back and forth past TDC, noting the highest reading on the indicator. Record this reading. 20 Repeat this measurement procedure on No 4 piston, then turn the crankshaft half a tur (180°) and repeat the procedure on Nos 2 and 3 pistons (see Iustration).

`citroen_xsara_en_1fd12d51` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:644 | doc_type:owners_manual
2Carefully examine the cylinder head boits for signs of damage to the threads or head, and for any sign of corosion. If the boits are in a satisfactory condition, measure the length of each boit from the underside of the head, to the and of the shank. The boits may be reused providing that the measured length does not exceed 133.3 mm. Note: Considening the stress to which the cylinder head bolts are subjected, it is highly recommended that they are all renewed, regardless of their apparent condition.

If the expansion tank filer cap must be removed before the engine and radiator have fuilly cooled (even though this is not recommended), the pressure in the cooling system must first be relieved. Cover the cap with a thick layer of cioth to avoid scalding, and slowly unscrew the filer cap until a hissing sound is heard. When the hissing has stopped, indicating that the pressure has reduced, siowly unscrew the filler cap until it can be removed; if more hissing sounds are heard, wait until they have stopped before unscrewing the cap. On restarting. this may lead to the engine running/idling roughly for a short while, until the ECU has relearned the optimum settings. 13 The heat shieids are secured to the underside af the body by various nuts and boits. Each shield can be remaved once the relevant exhaust section has been removed. If a shield is being removed to gain access to a component located behind it, it may prove

### General information
`citroen_xsara_en_d8eaba4a` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:912 | doc_type:owners_manual
1 All diesel engines covered in this Chapter utise slectronic control of certain functions. The number and type of sensors, actuators and associated components used on a particular engine depends on the engine type. territory of export and emission level. The tollowing information is therefore provided as a general guide to the components that may be encountered, according to engine type.

### Electronic Control Unit (ECU)
`citroen_xsara_en_9af30aff` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:913 | doc_type:owners_manual
2 An ECU is used on DHV (XUD9BSD engine) modeis to contral the injection timing. preheater glow plug operation and the exhaust gas recirculation system. The ECU receives signals from sensors, which monitor engine coolant temperature, engine speed. fuel injector operation and engine load. These signals are used by the ECU to control the previously mentioned system functions.

### Crankshaft sensor
`citroen_xsara_en_b8b9c661` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:914 | doc_type:owners_manual
3 This is an inductive pulse generator balited to the transmission bellhousing, to scan a reference ridge on the flywheeil. As the ridge passes the sensor tip, a signal is generated, which is used by the ECU, or the EGR system, to determine engine speed. The crankshaft sensor is used on ai engines.

### Coolant temperature sensor/switch
`citroen_xsara_en_f49cdfbd` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:915 | doc_type:owners_manual
4 The coolant temperature sensor is an NTC (Negative Temperature Coefficient) thermistar - that is, a semi-conductor whose electrical resistance decreases as its temperature increases. The sensor supplies a constantlyarying(analogue)voltage signal. corresponding to the temperature of the engine coolant. The sensor is used for control of the EGR system and preheating system and, on HV (XUD9BSD engine) models, is aiso used to refine the calculations made by the ECU when determining fuel metering. On some modets, the sensar consists simply of a switch whose internal contacts close once a predetermined coolant temperature has been attained.

### Throttle position switch
`citroen_xsara_en_772ba73d` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:916 | doc_type:owners_manual
5 The throttle position switch is fitted to all except DHV (XUD9BSD engine) models, and s located on the top of the injection pump.

### Throttle position sensor
`citroen_xsara_en_fe7c32a7` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:917 | doc_type:owners_manual
6 The throttle position sensor is used on DHV (XUD9BSD engine) modeis, and is located on the top of the injection pump, attached to the pump control lever. The unit consists of a potentiometer whose resistance varies according to accelerator position. From this information, the ECU can regulate the fuel injection timing according to driver input and engine load.

### Injector needle lift sensor
`citroen_xsara_en_6b334ac8` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:918 | doc_type:owners_manual
7 The needie lift sensor, used on DHV (XUD9BSD engine) models, is an integral part of No 3 fuel injector, and sends a signal to the ECU whenever the injector opens.

### Preheating system control unit
`citroen_xsara_en_5672b93c` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:919 | doc_type:owners_manual
This unit is fitted to all models and operates the preheating system giow plugs during cold staring conditions. On DHV (XUD9BSD engine) modeis, the unit is controlled by the ECU.

### General information
`citroen_xsara_en_50d4dc28` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:932 | doc_type:owners_manual
The fuel system consists of a rear-mounted fuel tank and fuel lift pump. a fuel cooler mounted under the car, a fuel titer with integral water separator, and a turbocharged, slectronically-controled High pressure Diesel injection (HD) system.

### System operation
`citroen_xsara_en_d37b5ae2` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:933 | doc_type:owners_manual
For the purposes of describing the operation of a common rail injection system, the components can be divided into three sub-systems; the low-pressure fuel system, the high pressure fuel system and the electronic control system.

### Low-pressure fuel system
`citroen_xsara_en_ebc6a90e` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:934 | doc_type:owners_manual
The low-pressure fuel system consists of the following components:

### High pressure fuel system
`citroen_xsara_en_99dc80f8` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:935 | doc_type:owners_manual
The high pressure fuel system consists of the following components:

dj High pressure fuel ines.

### Electronic control system
`citroen_xsara_en_cc61349a` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:936 | doc_type:owners_manual
The electronic control systern consists of the following components:

### Fuel lift pump
`citroen_xsara_en_d2c5a5b8` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:937 | doc_type:owners_manual
The fuel Iit pump and integral fuel gauge sender unit is electrically-operated, and is mounted in the fuel tank.

### High pressure pump
`citroen_xsara_en_11d419d3` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:938 | doc_type:owners_manual
The high pressure pump is mounted on the engine in the position normally occupied by the conventional distributor fuel injection pump. The pump is driven at half engine speed by the timing belt, and is lubricated by the fuel which it pumps.

### Accumulator rail
`citroen_xsara_en_cf4ecb48` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:939 | doc_type:owners_manual
As its name suggests, the accumuliator rail acts as an accumulator, storing fuel and preventing pressure fluctuations. Fuel enters the rail from the high pressure pump, and each injector has its own connection to the rail. The fuel pressure sensor is mounted in the rail, and the rail also has a connection to the fuel pressure control valve on the pump.

### Pressure control valve
`citroen_xsara_en_20d554cb` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:940 | doc_type:owners_manual
The pressure control valve is operated by the ECU, and controis the system pressure. The vaive is integral with the high pressure pump and cannot be separated.

### Fuel pressure sensor
`citroen_xsara_en_dd6c558b` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:941 | doc_type:owners_manual
The fuel pressure sensor is mounted in the accumulator rall, and provides very precise information on the fuel pressure to the ECU.

### Fuel injector
`citroen_xsara_en_f88e6103` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:942 | doc_type:owners_manual
The injectors are mounted on the engine in a similiar manner to conventional diesel fuel injectors. The injectors are electromagnetically-operated via signais from the ECU, and fuel is injected at the pressure existing in the accumulator ral. The injectors are high-precision instruments and are manufactured to very high tolerances.

Five separate forces are essential to the operation of the injector.

### ECU and sensors
`citroen_xsara_en_7f963953` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:943 | doc_type:owners_manual
The ECU and sensors are described earier in this Section - see Electronic controi system.

### General information
`citroen_xsara_en_6aaeba7d` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:984 | doc_type:owners_manual
All petral engines use unieaded petrol and alsa have various other features bult into the fuel system to help minimise harmful emissions. In addition, all engines are equipped with the crankcase emission control system described beiow. All engines are also equipped with a catalytic converter and an evaporative emission control system. 1.4 litre engines to emission standard L.4, aiso utise a secondary air injection system to quickly bring the catalytic converter up to naral working temperature.

The emission control systems function as follows.

### Crankcase emission control
`citroen_xsara_en_493e5eb9` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:985 | doc_type:owners_manual
To reduce the emission of unburned hydrocarbons from the crankcase into the atmosphere, the engine is sealed and the biow-by gases and oil vapour are drawn from inside the crankcase, through a wire mesh oi separator, into the iniet tract to be burmed by the engine during normal combustion.

### Exhaust emission control
`citroen_xsara_en_161b7c1a` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:986 | doc_type:owners_manual
To minimise the amount of pollutants which escape into the atmosphere, all models are fitted with a catalytic converter in the exhaust system. The system is of the closed-loop type, in which one or two lambda sensors in the exhaust system provides the engine management ECU with constant feedback. enabling the ECU to adjust the airfuel mixture ratio to provide the best possibie conditions for the converter to operate.

### Evaporative emission control
`citroen_xsara_en_5a6b1474` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:987 | doc_type:owners_manual
To minimise the escape into the atmosphere of unburned hydrocarbons, an evaporative emission control systerm is fitted to all models. The fuel tank filer cap is sealed and a charcoal canister is mounted undereath the right-hand wing to collect the petrol vapours generated in the tank when the car is parked. It stores them until they can be cleared from the canister (under the control of the engine management ECU) via the purge vaive into the inlet tract to be burned by the engine during normal combustion.

### Secondary air injection
`citroen_xsara_en_0d6511c8` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:988 | doc_type:owners_manual
Later 1.4 litre engines to emission standard L4 are also equipped with a secondary air injection system, This system is designed to reduce exhaust emissions in the period between first starting the engine, and unti the catalytic converter reaches operating (functioning) temperature. introduction of air nto the exhaust system during the initial startup period, creates an 'atterbumer' effect whicn quickly increases the temperature in the exhaust system front pipe, thus bringing the catalytic converter up to normal operating temperatures very quickly.

### Crankcase emission control
`citroen_xsara_en_f51da32f` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:989 | doc_type:owners_manual
To reduce the emission of unburned hydrocarbons from the crankcase into the atmosphere. the engine is sealed and the blow-by gases anid oil vapour are drawn from inside the crankcase, through a wire mesh oil separator, into the iniet tract to be bured by the engine during normal combustion.

### Exhaust emission control
`citroen_xsara_en_9a9b4c2f` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:990 | doc_type:owners_manual
To minimise the level of exhaust pollutants released into the atmosphere, a catalytic converter is fited in the exhaust system of all models.

### Exhaust gas recirculation system
`citroen_xsara_en_c60f4bee` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:991 | doc_type:owners_manual
This system is designed to recirculate smal quantities of exhaust gas into the inlet tract. and therefore into the combustion process. This process reduces the level of oxides of nitrogen present in the final exhaust gas which is released into the atmosphere.

### 4Catalytic converter - general information and precautions
`citroen_xsara_en_a867bde9` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1004 | doc_type:owners_manual
simple device which needs no maintenance in itself, but there are some facts of which an owner should be aware if the converter is to function properly for its full service Sife.

### Petrol engines
`citroen_xsara_en_41667027` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1005 | doc_type:owners_manual
a DO NOT use leaded petrol in a car equipped with a catalytic converter - the lead wil coat the precious metals, reducing their canverting efiency and will eventualy destroy the converter.   
Always keep the ignition and fuel systems wed-maintained in accordance with the manufacturer's schedule.   
if the engine deveiops a misfire, do no drive the car at al for at least as little as possible) unti the fault is cured.   
d DO NOT pushor tow-start the car - this willsoak the catalytic converter in unbumed fuel, causing it to overnheat when the engine does start.   
DO NOT switch off the ignition at high engine speeds.   
DO NOT use fuel or engine ol additives - these may contain substances harmful to the catalytic corverter.   
g DO NOT continue to use the car if the engine bums ail to the extent of leaving a visible trai of blue smoke.   
n) Remember that the catalytic converter operates at very high temperatures. DO NOT, therefore, park the car in dry undergrowth, over long grass or piles of dead leaves after a long run.   
Remember that the catalytic converter is FRAGILE - do not sthke it with tools during servicing work.   
In some cases a sulphurous smel (like that of rotten eggs may be noticed from the exhaust. This is common to many catalytic converter-equipped cars and once the car has covered a few thousand miles the problem should disappear.   
The catalytic converter, used on a welmaintained and well-driven car, should las for between 50 000 and 100 000 miles - if the corverter is no longer effective it must be renewed.

Note that the specific gravity readings assume an electrolyte temperature of 15°C (60\*F); for every 10°C (18\*F) below 15°C (60°F) subtract 0.007. For every 10°C (18"F) above 15°C (60F) add 0.007.

### Early 1.4 and 1.6 litre engines, and all 1.8 litre (8-valve) engines
`citroen_xsara_en_d69754cd` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1036 | doc_type:owners_manual
The ignition system is integrated with the fuel injection system to form a combined engine management system under the control of one ECU (See Chapter 4A for further information), The ignition side of the system is of the static (distributorless) type, consisting only of two twin-output ignition coils. The ignition coils are housed in a single unit. mounted on the left-hand end of the cylinder head; four HT leads connect the coil output terminais to the spark plugs.

### Later 1.4 and 1.6 litre engines, and all 1.8 and 2.0 litre (16-valve) engines
`citroen_xsara_en_6ae25763` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1037 | doc_type:owners_manual
On these modeis, the ignition side of the system is aiso of the static (distributoriess) type and operates as described previousty. The primary difference is that the ignition coils are housed in a single unit mounted directiy above the spark plugs. The coils are integral with the spark plug caps and are pushed directly onto the spark plugs, one for each plug. This removes the need for any HT leads connecting the cois to the plugs.

### Ignition system – testing
`citroen_xsara_en_ac4bd6a2` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1038 | doc_type:owners_manual

If necessary, the system wiring and wiring cannectors can be checked as described in Chapter 12 ensuring that the ECU wiring connectoris) have first been disconnected.

Overhauling a manual transmission is a difficult and involved job for the DiY home mechanic. In addition to dismanting and reassembling many small parts, clearances must be precisely measured and, i necessary. changed by selecting shims and spacers. internal transmission components are aiso often difficult to obtain, and in many instances, extremely expensive. Because of this, if the transmission develops a fault or becames noisy, the best course of action is to have the unit overhauled by a speciatist repairer, or to obtain an exchange reconditioned unit.

### AL4 type transmission
`citroen_xsara_en_fd074628` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1095 | doc_type:owners_manual
The AL4 transmission, optionally availabie on later 1.6 litre petrol engine modeis, is a development of the earler 4 HP 14 unit, and incorporates electronic control; the automatic gearchanges are electronically-controlled, rather than hydraulically as with the 4 HP 14 type. The advantage of electronic management is to provide a faster gearchange response. A kickdown facility is also provided, to enable a faster acceleration response when required.

### General information
`citroen_xsara_en_949d12da` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1116 | doc_type:owners_manual
1The starter inhibitor/reversing light switch is a dual-function switch which is screwed into the top of the transmission housing. The inhibitor function of the switch ensures that the engine can only be started with the selector ever in either the N or P positions, therefore preventing the engine being started with the transmission in gear. This is achieved by the switch cutting the supply to the starter motor solenoid. If at any time it is noted that the engine can be started with the seiector lever in any position other than P or N, thenit islikely that the inhibitor function of the switch is suspect. The braking system is of the servoassisted. dual-circuit hydraulic type. The arrangement of the hydraulic system is such that each circuit operates one frant and one rear brake from a tandem mastèr cylinder. Under normal circumstances. both circuits operate in unison. However, in the event of hydraulic failure in one circuit, full braking force will til be aaable at two wheels.

On ali modelis, the handbrake provides an independent mechanical means of rear brake application.

### General information
`citroen_xsara_en_97461970` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1292 | doc_type:owners_manual
The bodyshel is made of pressed-steel sections, and is available in three-door Coupe, five-door Hatchback, and five-door Estate versions. Most components are weided together, but some use is made of structural adhesives. The front wings are bolted on.

### 2 Maintenancebodywork and underframe
`citroen_xsara_en_614dc5ff` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1293 | doc_type:owners_manual
The general condition of a vehicie's bodywork is the one thing that significantly affects its value. Maintenance is easy, but needs to be regular. Neglect. particuiarly after minor damage, can lead quickly to further deterioration and costly repair bilis. It is important also to keep watch on those parts of the vehicle not immediately visible, for instance the underside, inside all the wheelarches, and the lower part of the engine compartment.

### 3 Maintenanceupholstery and carpets
`citroen_xsara_en_53c28ddc` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1294 | doc_type:owners_manual
Mats and carpets should be brushed or vacuum-cieaned regularly, to keep them free of grit. if they are badly stained, remove them from the vehicie for scrubbing or sponging. and make quite sure they are dry before refitting, Seats and interior trim paneis can be kept clean by wiping with a damp cloth and a proprietary upholstery cleaner. If they do become stained (which can be more apparent on light-coloured upholstery), use a littleliquid detergent and a soft nail brush to scour the grime out of the grain of the material. Do not forget to keep the headlining clean in the same way as the uphoistery. When using liquid cleaners inside the vehicle, do not overwet the surfaces being cleaned. Excessive damp could get into the seams and padded interior, causing stains, offensive odours or even rot. If the inside of the vehicle gets wet accidentally, it is worthwhile taking some trouble to dry it out properly, particularly where carpets are involved.

Caution: Do not leave oll or electric heaters inside the vehicie for this purpose.

Minor body damage - repair

вЩ

### Repairs of minor scratches in bodyworkork
`citroen_xsara_en_de7799ba` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1295 | doc_type:owners_manual
It the scratch is very superficial, and does not penetrate to the metal of the bodywork. repair is very simple. Lightly rub the area of the scratch with a paintwork renovator, or a very fine cuting paste, to remove laose paint trom the scratch, and to ciear the surrounding bodywork of wax polish. Rinse the area with clean water.

### Repairs of dents in bodywork
`citroen_xsara_en_271df3b6` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1296 | doc_type:owners_manual
When deep denting of the vehicle's bodywork has taken place, the first task is to pull the dent out, unti the affected bodywork aimost attains its original shape. There is litle point in trying to restore the original shape completely, as the metal in the damaged area wil have stretched on impact, and cannot be reshaped fully to its original contour. It is better to bring the level af the dent up to a point which is about 3 mm below the level of the surrounding bodywork. In cases where the dent is very shalliow anyway, it is not worth tying to pul it out at al if the underside of the dent is accessible, it can be hammered out gently from behind, using a mallet with a wooden or plastic head. Whilst doing this. hoid a suitable block of wood firmly against the outside of the panei, to absorb the impact from the hammer blows and thus prevent a large area of the bodywork from being "belledour'.

To complete the repair, see the Section on iling and respraying.

### Repairs of rust holes or gashes in bodyworrk
`citroen_xsara_en_4b9ef171` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1297 | doc_type:owners_manual
Remove all paint from the affected area, and from an inch or so of the surrounding 'sound' bodywork, using an abrasive pad or a wire brush on a power dil. If these are not available, a few sheets of abrasive paper will do the job most effectively. With the paint removed, you will be abie to judge the severity of the corrosion, and therefore decide whether to renew the whole panel (if this is possibie) or to repair the affected area. New body panels are not as expensive as most people think, and it is often quicker and more satisfactory to fit a new panel than to attempt to repair large areas of corosion.

### Bodywork repairs – filing and respraying
`citroen_xsara_en_5067bef1` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1298 | doc_type:owners_manual
Before using this Section, see the Sections on dent, minor scratch, rust holes and gash repairs.

### 5Major body damage - repair
`citroen_xsara_en_2d73cfde` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1300 | doc_type:owners_manual
Where serious damage has occurred, or large areas need renewal due to neglect, it means that compiete new panels will need weiding-in, and this is best left to professionals. If the damage is due to impact, it wil also be necessary to check completely the alignment of the bodyshel, and this can only be carried out accurately by a Citroen deasier, or accident repair specialist, using special jigs. If the body is left misaligned, it is primarily dangerous, as the car will not handie properly, and secondly, uneven strasses will be imposed on the steering, suspension and possibly transmission, causing abnormal wear, or complete failure, particularly to such items as the tyres.

### Waring: Before carrying out any work on the electrical system, read through the precautions given in 'Safety first at the beginning of this manual, and in Chapter 5A.
`citroen_xsara_en_8c78de6d` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1399 | doc_type:owners_manual
The electrical system is of 12-volt negative earth type. Power for the lights and all electrical accessories is supplied by a leadacid type battery, which is charged by the atternator.

### Electrical fault indinggeneral information
`citroen_xsara_en_95a6af6b` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1400 | doc_type:owners_manual
Note: Refer to the precautions given in "Safety first' and in Section 1 of this Chapter before starting work. The foilowing fests relate to testing of the main electrical circuits, and should not be used to test delicate electronic circuits (such as engine management systems or anti-lock braking systems), particularly where an electronic control unit is used.

### General
`citroen_xsara_en_025b1c3c` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1401 | doc_type:owners_manual
1 A typical electrical circult consists of an electrical component, any switches, relays. motors, fuses, fusible links or circuit breakers related to that component, and the wiring and connectors which ink the component to both the battery and the chassis. To heip to pinpoint a probiem in an electrical circuit. wiring diagrams are included at the end of this Chapter.

### Finding an open-circuit
`citroen_xsara_en_49d544d9` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1402 | doc_type:owners_manual
9 To check for an open-circuit, connect one lead of a circuit tester or voitmeter to either the negative battery terminal or a known good earth.

13 Cantinue to check the remainder of the circuit in the same fashion.

### Finding a short-circuit
`citroen_xsara_en_06d310e4` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1403 | doc_type:owners_manual
15 To check tor a short-circuit, first disconnect the load(s) from the ciroult foads are the components which draw current from a circuit, such as bulbs, motors, heating elements, etc.

### Finding an earth fault
`citroen_xsara_en_2aa239d5` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1404 | doc_type:owners_manual
20 The battery negative terminal 1s connected to 'earth' - the metal of the engine/transmission and the car body - and most systems are wired so that they only receive a positive feed, the current returming via the metal of the car body. This means that the component mounting and the body form part of that circuit. Loose or corroded mountings can therefore cause a range of electrical faults, ranging from total failure of a circuit, to a puzzing partial fault. In particular, lights may shine dimly (especially when another circuit sharing the same earth point is in operation), motors (eg wiper motors or the radiator cooling fan mator) may run slowly. and the operation of one circuit may have an apparently-unrelated effect on another. Note that earth straps are used between certain components, such as the engine/transmission and the body, usually where there is no metal to-metal contact between components, due to flexible rubber mountings, etc.

### 3.3a For access to the fuses, remove the cover from the interiar fuse/relay box ...
`citroen_xsara_en_0cc72619` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1405 | doc_type:owners_manual
use serrated washers between the terminal and the bodyshel, to ensure a clean and secure connection. When the connection is remade, prevent the onset of corosion in the future by applying a coat of petroleum jelly or silicone-based grease, or by spraying on (at regular intervals a proprietary inition seaer or water-dispersant lubricant.

20 Anti-theft alarm system and engine immobiliser general information

\*

### General
`citroen_xsara_en_f9358de3` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1457 | doc_type:owners_manual
All models in the range are fitted with an anti-theft aiarm system as standard or optional equipment. The alarm is automaticaly armed and disarmed using the remote central locking transmitter (where applicable), When the system is activated, the alarm indicator light, located on the facia, wll flash continuously. In addition to the alarm function, the system also incorporates an angine immobiliser activated by a transponder in the ignition key.

### Anti-theft alarm system
`citroen_xsara_en_c0541aad` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1458 | doc_type:owners_manual
Note that if the doors are operated using the key, the alarm will not be armed or disarmed (as applicabie),. If for some reason the remote central locking transmitter fails whilst the alarm is armed, the alarm can be disarmed using the key. To do this, open the door with the key, then anter the vehicle. noting that the alarm will sound as the door is opened. Switch on the ignitian, and once the ignition key is recognised, the alarm wil be disarmed.

### Engine immobiliser
`citroen_xsara_en_87c3368f` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1459 | doc_type:owners_manual
An electronic engine immobiliser is incorporated as part of the anti-theft system. The electronic immobiliser consists of a transponder fitted to the ignition key, and an analogue module fitted around the ignition switch. The system is controlled by the passenger compartment body computer.

### Disconnecting the vehicle batery
`citroen_xsara_en_83dbe523` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1460 | doc_type:owners_manual
Refer to Disconnecting the battery in the Reference Section of this manual).

21 Air bag system - general ifomation, precautions and system de-activation

### General information
`citroen_xsara_en_b0aa6884` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1461 | doc_type:owners_manual
A driver's air bag is fitted as standard equipment on certain models, and is an option an all other models. The air bag is fitted in the steering wheel centre pad. Additionally. a passenger's air bag located in the facia, and side air bags located in the front seats are also availabie.

### Precautions

aTransport the air bag by itsef, bag upward   
o not put your arms around the air bag.   
Cary the ar bag close to the body, bag outward.   
Do not drop the air bag or expose it to impacts.   
Do not attempt to dismantle the air beg unit.   
Do not connect any form of electrical equipment to any part of the air bag circult.

### Precautions to be taken when storing an air bag unit
`citroen_xsara_en_e8ce2784` | xsara | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:1465 | doc_type:owners_manual
a Store the unit in a cupboard with the air bag upward.   
Do not expose the air bag to temperatures above 80C.   
Do not expose the air bag to flames.   
Do not attempt to dispose of the air bag consult a Citron dealer.   
e Never refit an air bag which is known to be faulty or damaged.
